definition: The idea that the economy, like the government, should be run democratically: by and for the people who do the work, not for the profit of a few owners.
An economic system where the things society depends on, such as workplaces, housing, and energy, are privately owned and run for profit.
Everyone who has to work for a wage or salary to get by, plus the people who depend on them. That's most of us.
Standing with other working people because your struggles are connected, even when their fight isn't directly yours.
Workers joining together so they can bargain with their employer as a group over pay, hours, and conditions.
Negotiating a contract with an employer as a united group of workers rather than one at a time.
The ordinary members of a union or organization, as opposed to its staff or officers.
Neighbors meeting each other's needs directly, as equals. Solidarity, not charity.
Bringing people together around a shared problem and building enough collective power to fix it.
When a service or resource, such as a utility, a hospital, or housing, is owned by the public and run for people's needs instead of for profit.
A single public health plan that covers everyone, with no premiums, deductibles, or networks.
A plan to tackle the climate crisis by putting people to work building clean energy, transit, and housing, with good union jobs.
A vote by members to put the chapter's name, and sometimes its time and energy, behind a candidate or campaign.
A local DSA organization. Ours covers Placer, Nevada, El Dorado, and Sierra counties.
A local group within the chapter, organized around a town or area, where members meet face to face.
A team of members focused on one kind of work, such as elections or political education. Anyone can join one or start one.
What we call each other. It means someone on the same side, working toward the same thing.
